seoTitle: Fix Squarespace Domain Forwarding That's Not Working
metaDescription: Troubleshoot a Squarespace domain forwarding rule that isn't redirecting yet, from cache issues to leftover DNS records.
intro: Domain forwarding in Squarespace isn't instant — it can take anywhere from a few minutes to 48 hours to fully propagate, especially with SSL enabled. If your redirect still isn't working after a while, this guide walks through the most common causes and fixes.

steps.heading: Give it time first
steps.body: Squarespace notes that forwarding with SSL can take up to 48 hours to propagate, though most cases resolve within 1-2 hours.

steps.heading: Clear your browser cache
steps.body: Your browser may be holding old DNS or page data. Try an incognito tab or clear your cache and reload.

steps.heading: Test on another network or device
steps.body: If the redirect works on mobile or a different network, your local DNS is likely still catching up.

steps.heading: Check DNS records for leftovers
steps.body: Go to Settings, Domains, DNS Settings, and make sure there are no leftover A records or CNAMEs for the subdomain you're forwarding.

steps.heading: Confirm your rule and re-add if needed
steps.body: Verify the forwarding rule is saved correctly in Website, Forwarding, with the right URL and SSL enabled. If it's still not working, remove and re-add the rule.

faq.question: How long should I wait before troubleshooting forwarding?
faq.answer: Give it at least an hour or two, since propagation with SSL can take up to 48 hours in some cases.

faq.question: Why does clearing my cache help?
faq.answer: Your browser may still be showing an old cached version of the page or DNS lookup, which an incognito window or cache clear resolves.

faq.question: What if a leftover DNS record is causing the issue?
faq.answer: Even one leftover A record or CNAME on the forwarded subdomain can block the redirect from working — remove it in DNS Settings.

faq.question: Does removing and re-adding the rule actually help?
faq.answer: Yes, it can reset the redirect configuration and resolve cases where the rule appears saved but isn't functioning.
